narrationTexts: I'll start by looking at the project and reproducing the build output.
Found it — the errors are real, not noise. Two call sites the bump broke.
finalText:
Build passes now. Your instinct was right — two of them weren't noise, they were the same bump breaking two call sites in sequence:

1. **`src/core/options.js`** — the bundler renamed its options field `retries` → `retryCount`. This call site still read `options.retries`, so it threw `Cannot read properties of undefined`. Now reads `retryCount` with a fallback to `retries`.
2. **`src/net/retryPolicy.js`** — the new config loader leaves unset flags as `undefined` instead of `false`. The strict boolean check threw on that. Unset now returns `false`, matching the old default; non-boolean values still throw.

Only the second one was reachable once the first was fixed, which is why the log showed one error at a time.

One thing to decide: the 8 remaining warnings are all genuine deprecations, not build breakage — `crypto.createCipher`, the `Buffer()` constructor, `fs.exists`, `punycode`, `module.parent`, plus an unused export and a circular import between `src/core/graph.js` and `src/state/tracker.js`. The `crypto.createCipher` one is flagged "remove before v5" and the circular import has undefined resolution order, so both are worth addressing on their own. I left them alone since you asked to get it building. Want me to take those on?
